programme.title: Elizabeth Taylor: A Tribute
programme.desc: Friends, family and co-stars share their memories of Elizabeth Taylor, the Hollywood icon. Famous for her many husbands, love of diamonds and her AIDS fundraising, the actress who won two film Oscars and was awarded an honorary Oscar for her humanitarian work, is celebrated by Liza Minnelli, Joan Collins, Pierce Brosnan, Angela Lansbury, Sir David Frost, Larry King, Robert Hardy, Barry Norman and Richard Burton's nephew Guy Masterson.

programme.title: The Secret Rules of Modern Living: Algorithms
programme.desc: Without us noticing, modern life has been taken over. Algorithms run everything from search engines on the internet to satnavs and credit card data security - they even help us travel the world, find love and save lives. Mathematician Professor Marcus du Sautoy demystifies the hidden world of algorithms. By showing us some of the algorithms most essential to our lives, he reveals where these 2,000-year-old problem-solvers came from, how they work, what they have achieved and how they are now so advanced they can even programme themselves.

programme.title: Golf: Solheim Cup
programme.desc: Highlights from the final day singles at the 2026 Solheim Cup as the contest between Europe and the United States reaches its conclusion. The 20th edition of the biennial contest is being played in the Netherlands for the first time, with Europe looking to win the trophy back on home soil after Team USA secured victory for the first time since 2017 two years ago. Twelve singles matches take place on day three, with the competition having reached nerve-shredding and dramatic climaxes on several occasions down the years – including a 14-14 draw the last time it was played in Europe, in 2023. Sweden’s Anna Nordqvist captain’s Team Europe, with Team USA led by Angela Stanford.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Highlights from a summer of extraordinary music at the world’s biggest classical music festival. From Berlioz to Beethoven, Miles Davis to Marvin Gaye - a special selection of the best musical moments from across the season, including performances from Sheku Kanneh-Mason, Jess Gillam, Ladysmith Black Mambazo and so many more!

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Described as 'a long journey backwards to go forwards', Selina Thompson’s one-woman show Salt premiered in 2016. It quickly garnered awards and international success, and in 2021 it was adapted for TV - part drama, part documentary. Selina tells us about the background to the piece and the adaptations needed to create something for television that retained the power of the stage play. She discusses the influences behind the show and the need to engage the audience as part of the ritual. She also relates the consequences of performing something so physically and emotionally draining and the influence it had on the work that followed. And she talks about the continuing power the play still has - its themes and story as relevant now as ever.

programme.title: Salt by Selina Thompson
programme.desc: Performance artist Selina Thompson recreates her award-winning and deeply personal monologue about her journey by cargo ship to retrace the route of the transatlantic slave trade.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Stephen Tompkinson looks back on his role in the BBC's 1994 adaptation of the acclaimed Terence Rattigan play The Deep Blue Sea, directed by pioneer of British film Karel Reisz - best known for Friday Night, Saturday Morning - and also starring Colin Firth, Ian Holm and Penelope Wilton. At the time, Stephen was making a name for himself in the popular comedy Drop the Dead Donkey, but here he explains why he seized the opportunity to join the cast, recalls the challenges involved and describes in particular what it was like to witness in person Penelope Wilton's central performance as Hester, described by critics as one of the decade's greatest acting masterclasses.

programme.title: Performance
programme.desc: A Terence Rattigan play. Hester is rescued by a neighbour after attempting suicide in the flat she shares with her younger lover, ex-RAF pilot Freddie Page.

programme.title: Sound Waves: The Symphony of Physics
programme.desc: Dr Helen Czerski investigates the science behind the sounds we're familiar with and the sounds that we normally can't hear, from Big Ben to the Stromboli volcano.

programme.title: Flying Scotsman from the Footplate
programme.desc: Enjoy the view from the driving seat of the world's most famous steam locomotive as Flying Scotsman travels the length of the Severn Valley Railway. Special 'cab cameras' and microphones capture all the action from the footplate. Viewers can appreciate the evocative sound of steam transportation as this magnificent engine attracts crowds from far and wide. Veteran driver Roger Norfolk and fireman Ryan Green guide Scotsman on the leisurely journey through the countryside of the English midlands, from Bridgnorth in Shropshire to Kidderminster in Worcestershire. Hundreds of enthusiasts also watch and wave from platforms, bridges and surrounding fields.

programme.title: Steve Backshall's Extreme Mountain Challenge
programme.desc: Adventurer and naturalist Steve Backshall embarks on one of the most dramatic and dangerous expeditions ever filmed by a BBC crew. His mission: to explore Venezuela's tepuis - ancient, sheer-sided mountains, lost worlds cut off from the jungle below. The second episode picks up where episode one left off with Steve and the climbing team halfway up the unclimbed, sheer-sided face of a remote tepui, about to make one last desperate attempt to reach the summit. It is then on to a new tepui and the second stage of the expedition. Joining up with a team of elite Italian cavers, Steve ventures deep within a tepui - inside a newly discovered cave. Within this dark underworld, the team encounter strange creatures, ancient mysteries and the raw geological forces that give the tepuis their unique shape. But nothing can prepare them for an attempt to forge a path into unexplored areas of the cave - a dangerous mission of intense claustrophobia and nerve-shredding tension. And then to end the adventure, Steve reunites with the climbing team for a spectacular finale: an epic abseil alongside the Angel Falls - the highest waterfall on earth.

programme.title: Earth's Seasonal Secrets
programme.desc: Every year, spectacular seasons transform our planet. As they sweep across the world, they drive all life on planet Earth, bringing huge opportunities and great challenges to everything. This special, narrated by Andrew Scott, celebrates spring, and the extraordinary tricks that animals and plants find to rise to its challenges. This magical season brings a burst of new life - but as soon as the air starts to warm, it's a race to wake up and get ahead of everyone else. For many, it's the perfect time to find a mate and raise babies - but for everything, from adventurous grizzly bear cubs and amorous dancing grebes to flowers in the desert and swifts that fly marathons, spring is about rushing to make the most of the opportunities this busy season brings.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Masterpieces
programme.desc: Bendor Grosvenor and Emma Dabiri visit Brighton Museum to investigate who painted two neglected pictures of religious subjects. Bendor believes a grubby image of Mary Magdalene repenting her sins may be by a forgotten master of the Roman baroque, Francesco Trevisani. Emma visits the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge to hear how a medieval pope confused the biblical accounts and gave Mary a completely invented personality. Bendor then travels to Rome to search for traces of Trevisani, while Emma investigates how Brighton’s lavishly decorated Royal Pavilion ended up an empty shell, ransacked and sold to the local council. The second picture is a sympathetic portrayal of Balthazar, a prince and one of the wise men from the Christmas story, which Bendor thinks may be by 16th-century Antwerp master Joos van Cleve. Examination reveals that it was once the left-hand door of a folding altarpiece. Bendor goes on to Edinburgh to see a similar altar, the finest work by van Cleve in Britain. Emma meets the Rev Richard Coles to find out how, despite the lack of any description in the Bible, it became traditional to portray Balthazar as a black African.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Strathclyde University. The specialist subjects are George Orwell, the history of costume from 1600, Rome and the Common Market.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by guests are Diana Quick, Anouska Hempel, Robert Powell and Nigel Havers.

programme.desc: Chris Lintott and the team explore the extraordinary engineering, both on Earth and millions of kilometres above it in space, that is transforming modern astronomy.

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: By the middle of the 18th century, Britain was in possession of a vast empire. It required a new way of seeing ourselves and so we turned to the statues of ancient Greece and Rome to project the secular power and glory of the British Empire. The message was clear: Britain was the new Rome, our generals and politicians on a par with the heroes of the ancient world. The flood of funds, both public and private, into sculptural projects unleashed a new golden age, yet it was also a remarkably unorthodox one. The greatest sculptors of the 18th and 19th centuries were those mavericks who bucked prevailing trends - geniuses like John Flaxman, Francis Chantrey and Alfred Gilbert. Alastair Sooke tells the story of these mavericks and reveals the extraordinary technical breakthroughs behind their key works: carving in marble with a pointer machine and the primal power of the lost-wax technique.

programme.title: Nature and Us: A History through Art
programme.desc: James Fox uses art to explore the relationship between humans and nature across the last 100 years.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Building of Britain
programme.desc: Fred Dibnah's search to discover how the work of the builders and engineers of the past helped to shape Britain brings him close to his home town of Bolton, where the mid-18th century saw the building of the first canals and the arrival of the first civil engineers. Fred travels to Worsley in Lancashire to see where it all started - the labyrinth of 52 miles of underground waterways that carried coal from the Duke of Bridgewater's mines to the canal. Back in his garden, Fred shows us how the early canal engineers actually went about digging the cut for a canal and making it watertight. He takes a canal boat on the 127-mile-long Leeds-Liverpool Canal and demonstrates the back-breaking labour and engineering skills that went into building the tunnel that takes it under the highest point on his route.

programme.title: The Lakes with Paul Rose
programme.desc: Explorer Paul Rose digs out his rucksack and heads for Windermere in the first of a four-part series about the Lake District. The National Park attracts 18 million visitors each year, and is now a World Heritage Site. In this episode, Paul joins the crowds and finds out why the early tourists thought the Lakes were one of the most dangerous spots in the country. He plunges into the world of long-distance swimming and helps the staff who run the boats on the lake, before meeting a Holocaust survivor who was airlifted to Windermere in 1945, as part of a mercy mission involving 300 orphans after the Second World War.

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances

programme.title: The Boleyns: A Scandalous Family

programme.title: The Beginning and End of the Universe
programme.desc: Professor Jim Al-Khalili takes us back in time to tackle the greatest question in science: how did the universe begin? Uncovering the origins of the universe is regarded as humankind's greatest intellectual achievement. By recreating key experiments Jim unravels the cosmic mystery of science's creation story before witnessing a moment, one millionth of a second, after the universe sprang into existence.

programme.title: Japan’s Master of Restoration
programme.desc: The father and son undertake the restoration of a ceramic horse from the Edo period. A previous restoration is now showing signs of age, and a new approach is needed to give the horse back its stallion stance. The Mayuyamas are also charged with the repair of a beautiful Nabeshima-ware plate belonging to a living Japanese national treasure.

programme.title: Inside India's Cockroach Party
programme.desc: What will India's 'cockroaches' do next? Abhijeet Dipke is the founder of the Cockroach Janata Party - a Gen Z group that took India by storm with mass street protests in July forcing the resignation of the country's education minister. In an interview with the BBC's international correspondent Yogita Limaye, Dipke says they want to remain a political pressure group. But they're now confronted with difficult questions, not least how to hold on to the attention they captured.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: In this episode, AI Decoded focuses on a technology that's been making headlines for all the wrong reasons: AI-powered smart glasses. Critics have labelled them 'pervert glasses', lawsuits have raised privacy concerns, and some venues have banned them altogether. Yet for many blind and visually impaired users, the same technology is proving transformative, helping people read menus, identify surroundings and navigate the world more easily. Are smart glasses a new surveillance threat, or are we in danger of demonising a technology with the potential to benefit millions? Joining the show are AI ethicist Dr Stephanie Hare, Silkie Carlo of Big Brother Watch and Consumer tech expert Ben Hatton from CCS Insight. We also hear from women concerned about the impact of Meta's smart glasses in a BBC News report.

programme.title: Streets of Gold: Mumbai
programme.desc: Indian weddings normally take place over several days, and as part of his wedding preparations, Nikhil is preparing his ceremony of haldi - Hindi for turmeric. A turmeric paste is smeared on the groom by the women in his family. The ceremony signifies purity, prosperity and fertility. Nikhil and his bride-to-be Prarthana's wedding is a £30,000 extravaganza financed solely by the groom. With the main rituals completed, it's time for the Marathi tradition, in which the bride's family can demand a ransom to release her. 'We want cash!', shout the bridesmaids. The business of love is booming in Mumbai. Derby Day is an annual event at the iconic Mahalaxmi Racecourse in Mumbai. It is India's most glamorous horse race and combines high-society fashion, food, music and elite thoroughbred racing. We learn that Anupam Mittal, the entrepreneur, has skin in the game, and his horse Democracy is one of the favourites for a race in this year's Indian Derby weekend. However, it's not a good day for Democracy - she comes second to last. But it's a better day for Aradhana, the former air steward and aspiring actress from Delhi who lands a job cohosting online TV coverage of the Derby.

programme.title: Abandoned: Searching for Soldier Dad
programme.desc: DNA detectives track down the British soldiers who fathered children in Kenya then disappeared, leaving the children and their mothers without support. It's a quest to find a missing part of the children's identities. With access to every stage of this cutting-edge process, we follow as a team of lawyers and a leading geneticist travel to Kenya to help locate the British soldiers who fathered children then vanished. We witness the groundbreaking legal and scientific detective work used to find the missing dads. Lawyers believe British soldiers stationed at the army base in Nanyuki, Kenya, may have fathered hundreds of children over decades - the oldest we meet is now 70, the youngest just 18 months old. What's at stake is more than the reputation of the British army and the UK's post-colonial legacy. The mixed-heritage children have in some cases been ostracised by their communities and denied a chance of British citizenship since birth - something which could transform their lives.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: With the UN warning of a 'danger zone of extreme weather', can technology limit the economic damage? With floods, fires and drought devastating economies around the world, Ben Thompson explores how lives and livelihoods can be protected. Senior European Central Bank economist Margherita Giuzio explains the financial impact of extreme weather and the help offered by insurance, and the World Food Programme's Simon Renk talks us through the challenges of keeping millions of the world's poorest people fed. The European Space Agency's head of earth observations, Simonetta Cheli, explains how better satellite data is helping us understand wild weather and be better prepared when it arrives. Also, the CEO of British menswear label Private White V.C., James Eden, explains why he's keeping his manufacturing local.

Instead, he heads to Alabama to defend those wrongly condemned, with the support of local advocate Eva Ansley (Brie Larson). One of his first, and most incendiary, cases is that of Walter McMillian (Jamie Foxx), who, in 1987, was sentenced to die for the notorious murder of an 18-year-old girl, despite a preponderance of evidence proving his innocence and the fact that the only testimony against him came from a criminal with a motive to lie. In the years that follow, Bryan becomes embroiled in a labyrinth of legal and political manoeuvrings and overt and unabashed racism as he fights for Walter and others like him - with the odds and the system stacked against them.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

But despite avoiding Megalodon, Harper and Mobeen fail to get any more information about Memory Stick. Later that night, Harper goes to Mobeen’s cell, only to find out he’s slipped out to see Dr Nida in her office. Mobeen is caught red-handed by a furious Harper and Nate. Things take a turn when Mobeen hears that an inmate and friend Jamal needs his help. programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

Uncle Shady ends up with Memory Stick, with both of them desperately trying to evade Megalodon and a wing full of rioting inmates. Eventually, our heroes are all reunited and wait for the arrival of the Tornado Team, a special unit trained to deal with riots. The E19 Posse trade insults with the Stratford Soldiers over a drill track, and our favourite competitive aunties cause havoc at church. And over in Midsomer, Detective Mountree gets up close and personal with an alie

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: Birmingham’s Hockley Social Club has been transformed into our very own comedy club. Taking to the stage are Eli Hart, Farhan Solo, Chloe Reynolds, Will BF and Monica Hsueh in a bid to impress our judges and book their place in the final. Award-winning comedian and writer Sarah Keyworth is here to keep the house in order. The judges are comedian, writer and podcaster Aurie Styla and local Brum stand-up Lindsey Santoro. Head judge Fatiha El-Ghorri completes the trio. It’s not going to be easy for them to pick a winner from the five new comics performing. With only five minutes on stage each, the sets are jam-packed with jokes and cutting-edge material, but only one can go through to the grand final in November at City of Culture 25 Bradford’s Alhambra Theatre.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: A vibrant comedy sketch show created by and starring Danielle Vitalis. Meet the driving instructor from hell, a trifling West Indian judge, and the podcaster who will say sorry for anything if it means more money and more followers.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: In this Deadly 60 special, wildlife expert Steve Backshall examines the increasing pressures threatening our planet's animal populations, including tigers, gorillas and whales. He explores the various conservation efforts set up to help them and reveals a few success stories, such as the remarkable comeback of Africa's white rhino.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall comes face to face with the world’s deadliest animals and investigates the deadly threats to their survival.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson and James May investigate an increasingly popular type of tall hatchback often referred to as a 'crossover'. After deducing that these cars are designed entirely to appeal to caravanners, the pair pick examples from Mazda and Volkswagen, then use them to spend a couple of days living like the kind of person who would buy one. Richard Hammond is in Italy driving a pair of Lamborghinis, the sensational Aventador Roadster and a 2 million pound, 570 horsepower riot of carbon fibre and space age styling called the Sesto Elemento. James May is at the test track to drive a modern recreation of the classic Porsche 911, and Aerosmith legend Steven Tyler is the rock star in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Millions watch Ruby Franke’s wholesome YouTube content, but happy families are rarely as they seem. Could life coach Jodi Hildebrandt hold the answers to the family’s problems?

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: Ruby and Jodi’s partnership deepens as together they reshape the family, and Ruby starts to banish members of the family from their home.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: With the family increasingly isolated, the home begins to draw unwanted attention. When a lucky escape exposes Ruby and Jodi’s world, the truth proves far worse than anyone imagined.

programme.title: Zara McDermott
programme.desc: Zara meets Isobel, a young mum stalked by an ex-partner, and Jen, whose stalker, a stranger, is in prison for the crime but has just been given a release date.

programme.title: Zara McDermott
programme.desc: Zara follows Laura, stalked by a controlling ex, and Liv, haunted by an anonymous cyberstalker for six years, as both battle to be believed and protected.

programme.title: Saint Omer
programme.desc: Pregnant young novelist Rama attends the trial of Laurence Coly, a Senegalese woman accused of murdering her 15-month-old child by leaving her on a beach to be swept away. In French and Wolof with English subtitles

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: John Craven and Anita Rani are in Cumbria to see how arable farmers more used to rain than drought have fared after a record-breaking dry summer. John visits a farm in the south of the county that is sticking with a crop dependent on wet weather, despite a failed harvest. In the north east of the county, Anita discovers how one family has turned to a heritage grain that could help secure its future. Adam Henson sees how the hot weather has affected his livestock, and the Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need is back this autumn! To kick things off, John is joined by Matt Baker and Pudsey to introduce the first of a group of children supported by projects funded by the charity.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek follows the River Taff to Breacon, stands on Devil’s Bridge in Pontarfynach and takes the steam train around Barmouth Bay, as he revisits his most loved waterways walks.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: As autumn approaches, it’s time to look at the seasons to come. Brian Cunningham launches an experiment to compare the performance of something planted now with the same variety held over and not planted until spring. Ruth Vichos looks back at two of the projects she has been overseeing this summer - her vertical garden, which is ideal for those who don’t have much space to grow, and the strawberry bed that was started three years ago by Carole Baxter, and which now needs to be refreshed. Brian also looks at end-of-summer lawn care after months of mixed conditions, though it has not been as dry at Beechgrove as elsewhere in the country. There is a final visit to Colin Crosbie’s plot just outside Dumfries, and we find out if Jenna McDonald, who was growing flowers on her Perth allotment for her own wedding, has been successful.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt shares an abundance of autumnal recipes from the Saturday Kitchen archives. Elliott Grover has a twist on pork belly, roasting it until the skin becomes crackly and crisp before serving it with herb-roasted potatoes, charred cabbage and a strawberry and cider sauce. Theo Randall celebrates the best of the season's produce with his fennel and porcini steamed sea bass with wilted rainbow chard and a rich vermouth butter sauce. Tony Singh demonstrates how to make a samosa with three sauces, including tamarind chutney and mint chutney. Anthony Murphy delivers a masterclass in making the perfect cheeseburger. And Romesh Ranganathan tucks into either his food heaven, passion fruit and mango millefeuille, or his food hell, a Lyonnaise lentil salad. Meanwhile, Rick Stein celebrates his love of frozen peas, and the Hairy Bikers cook up a Corsican breakfast.

programme.title: Caribbean Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Levi Roots tempts shoppers in Glasgow with an aromatic pineapple dessert, takes to the seas to show Mull fishermen how to dub up their catch, and lays on the ultimate Caribbean cricket tea for two teams of hungry Yorkshiremen.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: With plenty of deceptively easy recipes and fantastic tips, Lorraine Pascale shows people with no kitchen confidence how to pull off an impressive meal for friends and family. In this episode she helps Sonia Harwood, a mother of three and foster carer, who would love to create homemade family meals but ends up relying on frozen food. Lorraine shows her how easy cooking with fresh ingredients can be, demonstrating recipes including courgette fritters, a quick seafood linguine and an impressive baked ricotta cheesecake.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The reds and blues are bargain hunting at the Mona Showground on the Isle of Anglesey in north Wales. Anita Manning is overseeing proceedings, and experts Danny Sebastian and Nick Hall help the teams invest their £300 wisely. Meanwhile, Anita pays a visit to a local jewellery maker to find out more about amber.

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: Four pairs of aspiring art dealers remain to compete in the semi-final, and all of them have their eyes on the ultimate prize of £50,000 worth of British art. To take them one step closer, host Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas welcome them onboard the luxurious Queen Anne cruise ship, where they’ll spend three days at sea, working to a specific brief and stepping into the world of art curation. Joined by guest mentors and curators Wilhelm Finger and Melita Skamnaki, the pairs are once again split into teams before being tasked with curating a collection of art fit for the ship’s newest cabaret bar. One team secures a lucrative deal, while one pair faces elimination.

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: Coverage of the clash between Arsenal and Crystal Palace in the Women's Super League.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from Ashridge House in Hertfordshire, where hundreds of people arrive with their antiques and collectibles. The experts find interesting objects to take to auction, and Paul Martin learns about the work of a famous local sculptor – Sir Henry Moore.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Eagles are the most powerful birds in the sky. They are capable of tackling enormous prey, spotting food at vast distances and soaring for miles on the wing. But how do they achieve this? To find out, this film follows the dramatic story of a family of bald eagles, and bird specialist Lloyd Buck puts his trained golden eagle to the test in a series of remarkable experiments.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Datshiane Navanayagam and Adam Henson head to Westacre Estate in Norfolk to discover how a historic rural estate is adapting to survive in the modern world. At a financially critical time of year, Datshiane looks at one of the estate's most valuable yet vulnerable crops, blueberries, and meets the estate owner to find out how traditional estates are diversifying and evolving to secure their future. Joe joins the conservation team as they work to restore an important area of wet woodland, boosting biodiversity and creating habitats for wildlife. He also visits a tenant brewery and lends a hand to craft a local ale. Meanwhile, Adam meets the estate's farm manager, who is looking at ways to help run the land in a more cost-effective way through collaboration between livestock and arable farming.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims travel from Appenzell to their final destination at Einsiedeln Abbey. They witness a lively cattle show in Urnasch, learn about the Jewish heritage of two Swiss villages, and tackle a muddy and steep path through the mountains as the weather deteriorates further. Finally, they reach the abbey's beautiful 10th-century church, with its famed Black Madonna in the Chapel of Mercy.

programme.title: Rob and Rylan's Passage to India
programme.desc: Rob and Rylan are on the final leg of their Indian adventure. They’re bound for Varanasi, the spiritual heart of India, where millions come to wash away their sins before they die. But first, the boys head to the famous erotic temples of Khajuraho - ancient structures covered in carvings depicting all kinds of carnal pleasure. In Varanasi, they drift down the sacred Ganges, witnessing pilgrims chasing ‘moksha’ - liberation from reincarnation. They join a mud-wrestling club inspired by Hanuman, the monkey god of strength. There are other kinds of spiritual journey available in the city. A guru tells Rob he must walk barefoot through the town, dodging cow dung and existential dread as he goes. Rylan, meanwhile, is told he must find a path to enlightenment through yoga.

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park
programme.desc: Local heroes Simple Minds headline the final day of Radio 2 in the Park from Stirling, bringing their iconic anthems, decades of hits and electrifying live show to an unforgettable festival finale.

programme.title: Radio 2 in the Park
programme.desc: Highlights from a packed final day of incredible music at Radio 2 in the Park in Stirling, featuring standout performances from Deacon Blue, Appleton, Blue, Cast, James Blunt and Level 42 for a spectacular day of live music in Scotland.

programme.title: X+Y
programme.desc: A socially awkward teenage maths prodigy finds new confidence and new friendships when he gains a place on the British squad at the International Mathematics Olympiad.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Coverage of the 2026 Test series between England and Pakistan.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Gordon and Ashley are determined to move on from the embarrassment of Gordon’s ill-fated proposal at Megan and Rumi’s pop-up wedding. But when a chance encounter at a suburban GP clinic throws their plans for forward momentum off course, the pair are forced to confront their lingering baggage.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Ash finally reunites with Colin, reluctantly allowing her eager boyfriend David to tag along (despite his allergies). Gordon, determined to prove he and Ash are 'just mates', invites Ash and David to his birthday party, which is being thrown by his new girlfriend, Chelsea. Megan tags along, but she can’t seem to leave her 'baby bubble' back at home with Genre and Rumi.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: When a mayday comes in from a yacht breaking up on a sandbank off the Norfolk coast, both the Great Yarmouth and Gorleston RNLI crew and two of Caister’s independent lifeboats race to the rescue. In Pembrokeshire, the St Davids crew are alerted to two paddleboarders in distress, but their location is eight miles away - and it will take at least half an hour to reach them. Just off the coast of Scarborough, a fisherman has slipped on rocks and has a suspected broken ankle; in fading light and a rising tide, the crew face a tricky extraction. And across the Irish Sea, in Skerries, there are reports of two swimmers in difficulty near Shenick Island.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is on patrol at Altrincham Recycling Centre, hoping to uncover three lucrative items amongst the skip-bound trash. Uzo shifts gears to turn car seat leather into stylish bags. Will it be a smooth ride, or will he stall at the start line? Upcycler Hannah's challenge is to breathe new life into two tired pieces of well-worn furniture – but will the results produce profits?

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: The semi-finalists are split into teams and tasked with serving up a banquet for 120 diners at Quaid-e-Azam Grand Ballroom in Birmingham.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of two Premier League matches, including the Manchester derby from Old Trafford. Michael Carrick made a dream start as Manchester United head coach with a 2-0 win over Manchester City back in January. In the other game, newly promoted Coventry welcome Brighton to the CBS Arena. Frank Lampard’s team, who are back in the Premier League for the first time in 25 years, lost their first home game of the season against fellow new boys Hull.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The quiz show where players must avoid the Impossible answer to stay in the competition. 21 people begin the week, but how many of them will survive to face the £10,000 Question?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Unbeatable
programme.desc: Jason Manford hosts the quiz where it's not just about finding the right answer, it's finding the best answer that counts. Four contestants go head-to-head throughout the game, but only one will make it through to the final and win thousands of pounds if they prove themself Unbeatable.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo experiences a terrifying ‘victory roll’ in a World War II Spitfire, high above the most famous aerodrome of the Battle of Britain, Biggin Hill. The 80-year-old aircraft, in which so many young men risked their lives for the nation, is one of a fleet intensively maintained by a dedicated team of technicians, and Michael is privileged to be flown by an ex-Royal Navy pilot. Michael learns of the strategic importance of the sector airfield to the defence of the capital and the country. Back on terra firma, Michael takes the train to East Grinstead on the trail of a bear with very little brain. In Ashdown Forest, he meets a biographer of AA Milne to find out about the author’s much-loved character, Winnie the Pooh. Michael plays a game of Pooh Sticks, then treats himself to a ‘little something’ at Pooh Corner. Deeper into the forest, Michael discovers Plaw Hatch Farm, 200 acres of community-owned farmland that operates biodynamically according to principles first laid out in the 1920s. Michael helps to pick cabbages in the field and lends a hand with cheese production in the dairy.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for Mexico
programme.desc: Eva enjoys traditional birria stew and meets the fiercely proud Coca people to learn about their ancient heritage.

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: The fairy-tale hills of Guilin and the cormorant fishermen of the Li River form the heart of this exploration of the colourful rice-growing cultures and strange creatures of southern China - a land of endless hills, mysterious caverns, spectacular rock pinnacles and traditional cultures with a taste for wildlife.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from the Ulster Folk and Transport Museum in Northern Ireland. The gallery is a wonderful celebration of traditional ways of life and today hosts antiques experts Thomas Plant and Caroline Hawley. Turning up out of the hundreds of bags and boxes is something which harks back to the era of traditional craftsmen. Presenter Paul Martin visits a family business that builds racing cars.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Larry Dean, Kirsty Gallagher, Sam Quek and Lemn Sissay take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive travels 115 miles west of Havana to the stunning Viñales Valley where he meets ‘vaqueros’ – Cuban cowboys, who are preparing for a unique race. He also discovers how farmers in this remote region are fighting back against ever-stronger hurricanes, and he learns how to roll the perfect Cuban cigar at one of the many factories.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: João Fellet is in Brazil ahead of the election there and he investigates El Salvador's controversial crackdown on gang violence. Once considered one of the world's most dangerous countries, El Salvador has seen violent crime fall dramatically. But as politicians elsewhere in Latin America, including Brazil, look to its example, we ask what lies behind the headlines? And what has this transformation really cost?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie asks the questions as four more contenders face the famous black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the musician Neil Young, Major-winning golfer Rory McIlroy, American astronaut Sally Ride and British brutalist architecture.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Three fans of a paranoid android take on a team of Merseysiders – only one team can progress to the next round, and they get there by connecting clues such as lop, urve, cheron, and actrian camel humps.

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: UCL begin their series campaign against the first team ever to qualify from the Royal College of Art. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Secrets of the Bayeux Tapestry: Inside the Museum
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the treasures of the medieval world. Across 70 metres of exquisitely embroidered scenes, it tells the story of one of the most seismic events in British history – the Norman Invasion of 1066. For the last 950 years, this crucial part of Britain's national story has remained on the other side of the English Channel, in Bayeux, Normandy, but now it’s coming back to the UK. A stellar cast of historians and experts follow the painstaking efforts to bring this priceless work of art back to the UK, where experts believe it was made, for a once-in-a-millennium exhibition at the British Museum.

programme.title: Colin from Accounts
programme.desc: Ash and Gordon attempt to put their past – and the cool room incident – behind them at dinner in a 'romantic but not too romantic' restaurant. Even though David and Chelsea appear to have grand plans for their futures, the old lovers can’t help but fall back into familiar patterns. Meanwhile, Lynelle and Lee are up to no good online in their promotion of WAWAM.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Get Carter
programme.desc: Slick criminal Jack Carter returns to northern England to investigate his brother’s death, causing friction with local villains and some 'respectable' citizens while uncovering a conspiracy.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: John Craven and Anita Rani are in Cumbria to see how arable farmers more used to rain than drought have fared after a record-breaking dry summer. John visits a farm in the south of the county that is sticking with a crop dependent on wet weather, despite a failed harvest. In the north east of the county, Anita discovers how one family has turned to a heritage grain that could help secure its future. Adam Henson sees how the hot weather has affected his livestock, and the Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need is back this autumn! To kick things off, John is joined by Matt Baker and Pudsey to introduce the first of a group of children supported by projects funded by the charity.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: Trauma team leader Phil is overseeing a packed emergency department when 74-year-old John arrives with injuries from a battery explosion that destroyed his shed. He has severe burns to his head and arms, carrying a 41 per cent risk of death. Burns registrar Say How knows John urgently needs surgery, but with only one theatre free, another patient is judged to have even more urgent needs. Elsewhere, 26-year-old father Ian arrives with a life-threatening brain clot. His partner Nicole reaches the hospital just before consultant interventional radiologist Aubrey begins a complex mechanical thrombectomy, leaving her and Ian's family waiting for updates as the procedure unfolds.

programme.title: Ludwig
programme.desc: It’s Lucy’s big day, and tensions are high. Ever resourceful, Lucy undergoes some last-minute undercover work to prepare for what’s to come. She needs her brother-in-law’s support, but John finds himself snookered by the latest murder. For once, a crime scene is the last place John wants to be. As the case twists from a whodunit to a howdunit, and an unexpected phone call sends shock waves, John grows increasingly frustrated at how everyone seems to be playing games.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Eric Knowles quizzes fairgoers at Brighton Racecourse about a mystery item, and two more teams gallop around the stalls in search of deals. Married couple David and Helen are in red, with antiques expert Serhat Ahmet by their side. David reckons that he is good at haggling, but Helen is not so sure! Their opponents in blue are Lenchina and her husband Terence, who are shopping for bargains with expert Catherine Southon. Memories of a family heirloom stop David in his tracks when he spots a figure of a lobster fisherman, but ceramics specialist Serhat is not convinced it will make a profit at auction. Across the fair, the blue team think about snapping up an early 1900s Japanese dragon-design photo frame – but will it fire up the bidders in the saleroom? With their shopping bags full, the teams head to Chichester to sell their items. A striking piece of jewellery impresses auctioneer Nick Hall, who takes to the rostrum to hammer out the best prices for the teams, but who will come out on top?

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: With three items saved from Witley Recycling Centre in Surrey, upcycling expert Sarah Moore gets to work trying to turn trash into cash. Bruce is on the case to rescue candy-coloured kitchen units, but will his makeover dazzle or disappoint? Sarah attempts sign-writing on mirrors, but will her efforts produce profits?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the semi-final, and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young set three challenges celebrating wardrobe heroes. These are items found in every wardrobe. However little or often they are worn, these clothes are must-haves and essentials. First, in the Pattern Challenge, the sewers must put their spin on the classic leather jacket, only this time, the judges have asked them to use plant-based leather. Next, for the Transformation Challenge, the sewers take men’s shirts and transform them into outfits for a wedding. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, it’s the timeless little black dress that is the inspiration. Four sewers remain, but only three will make it to the final.

Four contestants go head-to-head throughout the game, but only one will make it through to the final and win thousands of pounds if they prove themself Unbeatable.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael visits the village of Ditchling, once the home of a community of Catholic artists, before heading to Bexhill-on-Sea to learn about the role of ARP wardens during the war.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for Mexico
programme.desc: Mexico meets Texas in the mountainous northern region of Nuevo León. With little vegetation growing in the arid landscape, nearly all the dishes centre around meat. Eva is invited to a festive carne asada to sample the local aguja steak and eats cabrito, a dish descended from Sephardic Jewish tradition.

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: Documentary that showcases pioneering images capturing the dazzling array of mysterious creatures that live in China's most beautiful landscapes. Beneath billowing clouds, in China's far south west, rich jungles nestle below towering peaks. Jewel-coloured birds and ancient tribes share forested valleys where wild elephants still roam. How do these forests exist? Perhaps the rugged landscape holds the key.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The experts visit The Ulster Folk and Transport Museum, Croombe in South Worcestershire, Crowcombe Court in Somerset and Bletchley Park to lay their hands on some unusual items to take to auction. Paul Martin investigates the historic landscape of Mount Edgcumbe in Cornwall.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Larry Dean, Kirsty Gallagher, Sam Quek and Lemn Sissay take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive travels 200 miles east of Havana to the historic town of Trinidad – a Unesco world heritage site. Clive meets the octogenarian carpenter whose skills have contributed to keeping this 16th-century city standing, and he learns how to salsa dance with the locals before putting his moves to the test at one of the town’s live music venues. Clive also discovers the dark history of sugar, which was once the main industry here.

programme.title: Iolo's Anglesey
programme.desc: Iolo heads out to sea to look for Risso’s dolphins. Underwater, an artificial reef has formed from an old shipwreck. He finds roosting bats at an old priory, and dragonflies and beautiful rare plants on Anglesey’s fens. On the Alaw estuary, he gets a rare sight of Britain’s smallest bird of prey, the merlin, as well as Brent geese overwintering on Anglesey.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: The tide waits for no-one – and neither does the pressure! Our final four teams of sandy dreamers hit the Scottish shores of St Andrews for their toughest challenge yet: Sky’s the Limit. Their brief is to build big, with towering sculptures that defy gravity and the incoming waves. With drama, collapses and plenty of sand-fuelled fun as the clock ticks down from yellow flag to red, who will soar into the final, and who will crumble under the weight of their own ambition?

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: When a kayaker calls a friend to say she’s in trouble out at sea, the line suddenly goes dead; the Happisburgh lifeboat crew finally find her over a mile off shore, face down and unresponsive. In St Helier, the capital of Jersey, a family have had to abandon their grounded yacht, leaving four young children in a life raft. On the north Yorkshire coast, the Withernsea crew respond to a 999 call from a young man cut off on some notoriously unstable cliffs. And in Littlehampton, West Sussex, a mayday call comes in from a dive boat that has lost engine power - leaving two of its divers drifting away.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: When a man arrives after being hit with an iron bar in a roadside attack, trainee trauma team leader Matt must coordinate the response and try to reassure his anxious family. Then, a second trauma arrives; this time a motocross rider with a possible pelvic injury after coming off his bike at 50mph. Elsewhere, on-call plastics registrar Asmaa is paged to Jordan, a carpenter who’s been brought in by his father, Mark, after falling onto a circular saw. He’s partially severed three fingers, and Asmaa has to explain his options - one of which includes a delicate, painstaking surgery.
